# A panel the program builds at run time reads a context its page never
# provides, through a function: the panel is handed the context's value as a
# prop, read where the panel is written.
#
# html declares a context's default as a binding of the page, and the lift
# rebuilt the read it hands the panel unmarked, so html read it off `state`,
# where nothing is: the page raised as it loaded.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import i18n "sngl:i18n"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// The language of the active locale, lower-cased.
func lowered() => string.lower(i18n.locale)

component page ui.node {
    var shown = true

    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #toggle(text="toggle", @click { shown = !shown })
        if shown {
            ui.text #lang(value=lowered())
        }
    }
}

ui.window {
    page()
}

func testAPanelReadsTheLocale(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.setContext(i18n.locale, "FR")
    t.assert(c.lang != null && c.lang.value == "fr")
}
